meta.device: dog (30.245.40.99), Jetson AGX Orin, TensorRT 10.7, pymunk 7.3.1, gym 0.26.2
meta.harness: eval_trt_pusht.py (ctypes, standalone PushTImageEnv + MultiStepWrapper logic replicated, no torch)
meta.config: DDIM-50, n_test=50 (env seeds 10000-10049), enc=obs_encoder_fp16, unet=unet_fp16 vs unet_int8
meta.noise: torch.randn(1,16,2, generator=manual_seed(s)) for s in 0..5, baseline-matched (numpy noise gives ~0 -- Push-T closed-loop is chaotic/noise-implementation-sensitive, see PROBLEMS P16)
meta.platform_caveat: dog absolute scores below pc-3070 onnxruntime baseline (0.814) due to pymunk 7.3.1 vs 6.2.1 + chaotic amplification; INT8-vs-FP16 is same-platform paired, valid

parity_context.note: TRT FP16 engine matches onnxruntime FP32 (1.2e-3); TRT INT8 diverges ~7-9% from FP16, amplified by chaotic closed-loop into ~0.12 score drop

conclusion: TRT native INT8 (entropy calibration) costs ~0.12 closed-loop accuracy vs FP16 on Orin (p<0.001, 6/6 seeds negative). Contrasts with onnxruntime QDQ INT8 (lossless on pc-3070). The two INT8 routes differ in quality; TRT INT8's ~7-9% action divergence is amplified by the chaotic + threshold Push-T dynamics.
